newsitem.title: USA: McGuire power plant to reopen mid-Nov-Duke.
newsitem.headline: McGuire power plant to reopen mid-Nov-Duke.

text.p: Duke Power Co said Friday McGuire 1 and 2 nuclear power stations are expected to return to service in mid-November.

In a quarterly filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the company said it expects to meet customer needs with a combination of other Duke Power generation and purchases of energy from neighboring utilities.
Duke shut down its McGuire facilities last month to replace battery banks, which are designed to supply backup power to instrumentation systems to the plant.
The Oconee nuclear station was also shut down last month for inspection and possible modification of piping systems, after a steam line on the non-nuclear side of the plant ruptured, the filing said.
As a result of the inspections, outage at the Oconee station is expected to continue through the end of the year, the company said in the filing.
Duke said it is of "the opinion that these outages will not have a material adverse effect on the results of operations or the financial position of the company."
Duke Power Co., based in Charlotte, N.C., has an overall generation capacity of about 18,500 MW, of which about 12 percent comes from the McGuire facility.
